quotes.for: November 22, 2026 publication date of Jakub Pachocki's essay Perplexity and Intelligence.

quotes.text: In this post, I argue for establishing perplexity (or, equivalently, cross-entropy loss) as a metric to compare between model developers and inform shared safety standards.
quotes.for: Pachocki arguing for cross-entropy loss and perplexity as a durable metric across model developers.

quotes.text: It would make little sense to evaluate GPT‑2 and GPT‑3 on most modern benchmarks; and the benchmarks used then were largely saturated around GPT‑4. In contrast, I believe looking at progress on pretraining is likely to stay informative.
quotes.for: Downstream benchmarks saturating quickly around GPT-4 while pretraining loss stays informative.

quotes.text: The primary held-out datasets we’ve been using since GPT-3.5 are sourced from our internal codebase, and those are the numbers reported here (for a fixed snapshot).
quotes.for: OpenAI's reported log-perplexity numbers are measured on a fixed snapshot of its internal codebase held-out dataset since GPT-3.5.

quotes.text: GPT‑3.5, at a log-perplexity of ~0.99 on our current main evaluation dataset, was capable of fluent conversation and formed the basis for the original ChatGPT.

quotes.text: For more than a year, we have been posing open problems in mathematics to our models as one of the ways of evaluating them.
quotes.for: OpenAI evaluating models on open problems in mathematics.

quotes.text: I don’t know what those capabilities will be, and we may not be testing for them today.
quotes.for: Pachocki acknowledging OpenAI may not be testing today for capabilities that emerge in the ~0.68-0.7 log-perplexity window.

quotes.text: That is, I’d like an industry standard that specifies a first limit on development, measured by some key metric we can track across labs, and what concretely we’d need to achieve before going beyond it.
quotes.for: Pachocki calling for an industry standard specifying a first development limit and concrete safety milestone without naming the threshold value.

quotes.text: Different developers use different evaluation datasets and train on different data mixtures. Here, we report the numbers on the main dataset we have been tracking
quotes.for: Structural limit of different evaluation datasets and training data mixtures across labs.

quotes.text: Most notably, chain-of-thought reasoning does not reduce perplexity achieved by the model, even though it leads to a drastic increase in capabilities.
quotes.for: Chain-of-thought reasoning boosting capabilities without lowering model perplexity.

quotes.text: We do not expect it is possible to achieve a loss of 0, which would correspond to being able to predict the dataset entirely deterministically. But we do not know what the inherent entropy of the data is.
quotes.for: Unknown inherent entropy floor of datasets.
